sentimento.text1: With 69 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), the week opened with fresh polling, and with the first national survey whose fieldwork sits entirely after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention. The [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) poll released on Monday (n=2,004, telephone, fieldwork Jul 24 to 26, 2pp margin, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing BR-01489/2026) puts Lula at 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 33% in the first round, with Caiado at 6%, Renan Santos at 5% and Zema at 3%, and 47% x 43% in the head-to-head runoff. Against the same institute's Jul 13 round, Lula gains 2pp and Flávio loses 1pp, both moves inside the margin, which widens the first-round gap from 6pp to 9pp. Rejection: Flávio 50% and Lula 48%.
sentimento.text2: The poll's finding is not about the top two, it is about Ronaldo Caiado. He is in a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) with Lula at 45% to 43%, the narrowest of the four runoff scenarios in the survey, ahead of Zema (46% x 42%), Flávio (47% x 43%) and Renan Santos (47% x 39%). That INVERTS the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24, published three days earlier, in which Lula beat Caiado by 47% to 40%, seven points, the widest cushion in that survey. Two top-tier institutes, with fieldwork two days apart, reach opposite conclusions about which challenger is the most competitive. The panel records the divergence and does not arbitrate which one is right.
sentimento.text3: In the market, the top stood still and the chasing pack moved. Lula stayed at 62.50% (vol USD 7.68M) and Flávio rose 0.20pp to 23.85% (vol USD 7.68M), with the gap at +38.65pp. Caiado was the one who moved: up 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 1.95% (vol USD 5.15M), and up in third place in the first round as well, from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50%, in the same direction the new polling pointed. A series correction the panel owes to anyone who read it yesterday: the ceiling of Lula's price in the AFOS series is not 62.50%, it is 63.50%, marked in the early hours of Jul 26, after the panel's capture, and the widest gap in the series is +39.80pp, from those same early hours. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.12M. CAPTURE CAVEAT, recorded because hiding it would be worse: the double-reading lock BLOCKED both of today's rounds, at 4:23pm BRT. In the first, the second-place and third-place books diverged; in the second, only Caiado's third place, between 19.00% and 19.50%. The presidential book returned IDENTICAL numbers across all four readings over 17 minutes, which is why the winner prices enter here as firm. The placement numbers enter as a range, not as a settled price.
sentimento.direita: Flávio rose 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 23.85%, but fell 1.50pp in second place in the first round, to 76.50%, and rose 0.75pp in third place, to 7.75%. His three books moved in different directions in the same session, the opposite of yesterday's clean reading. In the polling, [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) puts him at 33% in the first round, one point below the same institute's Jul 13 round, and keeps rejection as his ceiling: 50%, the highest in the survey, above Lula's 48%. The surrounding names kept retreating: Michelle fell 0.35pp to 0.40% (vol USD 9.29M) and Jair held at 1.05%. Away from the data, the story of the day: Folha de S.Paulo reported that fund managers, economists and executives speaking on condition of anonymity are hoping he withdraws in favour of Caiado, and senator Rogério Marinho, who coordinates the pre-campaign, replied to the piece publicly.
sentimento.esquerda: Lula stayed at 62.50% (vol USD 7.68M), unchanged against yesterday's capture, with the gap over Flávio at +38.65pp. The new polling has him at 42% in the first round, two points above the same institute's Jul 13 round, and winning all four runoff scenarios tested, though two of them sit inside the margin. The point to watch is approval: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) shows 47% approval against 49% disapproval, against 47% x 47% on Jul 13, while [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) on Jul 24 showed the reverse, 49% x 48%. Both carry a 2pp margin and both are [statistical ties](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico), so the honest reading is a narrow band around 48%, not a swing in either direction. On the administration, which is a different question, Nexus shows 36% excellent or good against 43% poor or terrible.
sentimento.terceiraVia: This was the chasing pack's day, and for the first time in two weeks polling and price converged. Caiado rose 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 1.95%, and went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50% in third place in the first round, on the same day [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) showed him in a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) with Lula in the runoff and at 6% in the first round, the best of the pack. Zema went the other way: he was formally nominated by [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) at a convention in Brasília, still without a running mate, and fell 0.10pp to 0.55% (vol USD 4.54M), with 3% in the new polling. Renan Santos held at 9.55% in the winner contract (vol USD 8.56M), but lost 2.50pp in third place, to 62.00%, and gained 0.80pp in second place, to 12.65%. Haddad fell 0.10pp to 0.25% and Michelle 0.35pp to 0.40%.
sentimento.polymarket: Lula 62.50% (flat, vol USD 7.68M), Flávio 23.85% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 7.68M), Renan 9.55% (flat, vol USD 8.56M), Caiado 1.95% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.15M), Jair 1.05% (flat, vol USD 5.25M), Zema 0.55% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 4.54M), Michelle 0.40% (down 0.35pp, vol USD 9.29M), Camilo Santana 0.40% (down 0.05pp), Haddad 0.25% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 6.38M), Alckmin 0.25%, Tarcísio 0.15% (flat, vol USD 13.64M), Tereza Cristina 0.15%. Lula's gap over Flávio at +38.65pp, down 0.20pp against yesterday's capture. Sub-markets: second place in the first round with Flávio at 76.50% (down 1.50pp) and Renan at 12.65% (up 0.80pp); third place with Renan at 62.00% (down 2.50pp) and Caiado between 19.00% and 19.50%, up 3.50pp to 4.00pp, published as a range because the lock did not confirm that book across two rounds. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.12M. Capture Jul 27, 7:23pm UTC. The presidential book returned the same numbers across all four readings of two lock rounds, over 17 minutes.

inss.text1: The fiscal agenda is still bottled up and produced no news on Monday: the Senate remains in recess, the government's priority bills went unvoted and Davi Alcolumbre is still holding back promulgation of the [pauta-bomba](/en/glossary#pauta-bomba) pending a conversation with Lula. The day's agenda was electoral and external, not legislative: the [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) convention, new polling, and the next chapter of the friction with Argentina, with China declaring support for Brazil against external interference amid the moves by Trump and Milei (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 27).
inss.text2: The market left the favourite's price untouched for a second straight session: Lula stayed at 62.50%, unchanged. But unlike yesterday, the day's movement was not confined to the fight between second and third place. It went to the chasing pack, and with polling behind it: Caiado rose in both books where he appears, on the same day a national poll showed him in a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) with Lula in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). When price and polling move together, the reading is stronger than when price moves alone, and it is worth recording that this convergence had not happened in his case for two weeks.
inss.text3: The [STF](/en/glossary#stf) impeachment market stood at 3.40% (vol USD 83 thousand), unchanged against yesterday, a fourth day essentially flat. The methodological caveat still weighs more than the number: with USD 83 thousand in accumulated volume, against USD 116.12M in the presidential market, this book is orders of magnitude smaller and movement in it does not support a narrative. What is worth recording is the absence of movement across a sequence now four days long that includes a foreign head of state attacking a justice from a Brazilian campaign platform, a public reply from the Court's president, an ambassador recalled for consultations and now a statement from China on external interference. Real money goes on treating all of it as friction, not as removal risk.
inss.text4: On the electoral front, Monday delivered the two things Sunday lacked: polling and movement in the chasing pack. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) measured the electorate after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention and [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) formally nominated Zema, closing three launches in three days. The week still brings three national polls with release dates filed at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse), the largest by sample being [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) on Jul 28, at n=5,000 with fieldwork from Jul 22 to 27, followed by PoderData on Jul 30 (n=2,400) and Vox Brasil on Jul 31 (n=2,100). A TSE filing is not a guaranteed release, and dates slip.
inss.impactoLula: The new reading is [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27: Lula's personal approval at 47% against 49% disapproval, with 4% who did not answer, against 47% x 47% in the same institute's Jul 13 round. Approval held and disapproval rose 2pp, inside the margin. The contrast with [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) of Jul 24 is the figure the panel records without arbitrating: there it was the reverse, 49% x 48%. Both surveys carry a 2pp margin and both are [statistical ties](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico), which describes a narrow band around 48% rather than a swing. The earlier ones: PoderData Jul 22 at 46% x 47%, Indexa Jul 21 at 49% x 48%, Real Time Jul 21 at 46% x 50%, Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) Jul 15 at 48% x 47% and PoderData/Aya Jul 16 at 42% x 51%.
inss.impactoGestao: The assessment of the ADMINISTRATION is a different question from personal approval, and the distance between the two remains the figure that matters: in [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27, 43% rate the government poor or terrible (9% poor and 34% terrible) against 36% excellent or good (15% excellent and 21% good) and 20% fair. Against the same institute's Jul 13 round, both sides rose, the positive from 35% to 36% and the negative from 41% to 43%. [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) on Jul 24 measured 32% x 38% x 28%, meaning the two institutes disagree on the level and agree on the sign: voters approve of the person more than they approve of the administration. On inflation, the market kept the modal band at 5.00% to 5.49%, priced at 39.20%, followed by the 4.50% to 4.99% band at 26.30% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band at 12.10% ([Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket)). The centre of the distribution remains above the target ceiling, with the whole book totalling USD 77 thousand.
inss.conclusao: With 69 days to the election, Monday delivered the test Sunday could not. The new polling confirmed the picture at the top, with Lula widening from 6pp to 9pp in the first round inside the margin, and stirred things below, putting Caiado two points from Lula in the runoff against seven points in the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll three days earlier. The market moved in the same direction on Caiado, who rose in both books where he appears, and in the opposite direction on Zema, formally nominated and falling in the same session, the third launch in a row to end that way. Lula held at 62.50% for a second day. What Monday showed, and Sunday could not, is that the fight for second place is settled neither in the polling nor in the price.

bancoMaster.text1: After a Sunday when the specific news query on the case came back empty, Monday brought something new, by an indirect route: a market story. Folha de S.Paulo reported that fund managers, economists and executives speaking on condition of anonymity view Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy with strong rejection, and that among the reasons cited is his having lied about his closeness to banker Daniel Vorcaro, of [Banco Master](/en/glossary#banco-master), from whom he asked for money. The piece rests on anonymous sources, it is not a finding by any authority, and it is recorded as what it is: reporting, not a court filing.
bancoMaster.text2: The procedural picture that still stands has two fronts that should not be conflated. On the asset side, the Rio courts ordered accounts frozen at [Banco Master](/en/glossary#banco-master), Trustee DTVM, Axor Asset and two partners, Alexandre Marchesani Canata and Felipe Mota Separovic Rodrigues, capped at R$ 135 million, in a ruling by judge Wladimir Hungria of the Public Treasury Court, at the request of the state and of Rioprevidência. The origin is a R$ 150 million allocation made by Rioprevidência into the Texas i Fia fund between July 4 and August 8, 2025, with the portfolio almost entirely exposed to Ambipar shares.
bancoMaster.text3: On the criminal side, the inquiry authorised by André Mendonça on Jul 23 into Daniel Vorcaro's payments for the film about Jair Bolsonaro continues, with corruption and money laundering in scope. On price, the honest record is that the causes cannot be separated: Flávio rose 0.20pp in the winner contract and fell 1.50pp in the second-place contract on the same day the Faria Lima story ran, a new national poll came out and a third candidate was formally nominated. Three events in one session do not allow the move to be attributed to any of them, and the panel does not attribute it.
bancoMaster.conclusao: The two fronts of the Master case continue to run on separate tracks and should not be added together: the criminal one, at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf), still under investigation, and the asset one, in the Rio courts, with a set amount and named defendants. Monday's development is not procedural, it is reputational, and it appears in a story about how the financial market reads the candidate. It is worth recording the coincidence that, on the same day, the name identified as that market's preference, Caiado, rose in both books where he appears, and worth recording just as clearly that coincidence is not cause and that the panel asserts none.

stf.toffoli: Toffoli remains isolated at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) after the Master crisis, with no new individual ruling captured on Monday.
stf.moraes: He was named as a target without having issued any new ruling, and the episode gained a further international chapter. After Javier Milei called him "bald garbage" from the platform of the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention on Jul 25, after [STF](/en/glossary#stf) president Edson Fachin replied publicly and after the Brazilian government recalled its ambassador to Argentina on Jul 26, the Argentine press reported on Monday that Milei will not apologise to Brazil (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 27). On the same day, China declared support for Brazil against external interference and Cármen Lúcia publicly defended democracy and criticised interference (Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Jul 27).
stf.gilmar: No individual action by Gilmar in the period. The recent joint vote stands, with Dino, Moraes and Zanin, which reduced restrictions on [penduricalhos](/en/glossary#penduricalhos).
stf.dino: No individual ruling from Dino in the period. A murder inquiry under his reporting duty became a weapon in the Maranhão election contest, according to Folha de S.Paulo of Jul 27. He remains a target of Bolsonarismo, and the recent joint vote on [penduricalhos](/en/glossary#penduricalhos) stands, with the budget dispute still open at the Court.
stf.mendonca: He remains the reporting justice in the Vorcaro case, having authorised the Federal Police on Jul 23 to open an inquiry into the banker's payments for the film about Jair Bolsonaro, with corruption and money laundering in scope. No new individual ruling captured on Monday.
stf.nexo: Monday's through-line stayed sovereign and gained a fourth beat. After Itamaraty denied visas to US officials, after the US government publicly denied any intent to undermine the Brazilian election, after Milei's attack on Moraes and after the ambassador in Buenos Aires was recalled, on Monday the Argentine press reported that Milei will not apologise and China declared support for Brazil against external interference. In parallel, [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) released a cut of its Jul 22 and 23 round (n=2,004) in which 52% say they believe Trump's tariff push is meant to favour Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy, against 37% who disagree and 11% who do not know, running at 73% among Lula voters and 29% among Flávio voters. The [STF](/en/glossary#stf) still leans towards blocking the [pauta-bomba](/en/glossary#pauta-bomba), with Alcolumbre holding back promulgation.
stf.analise: The market on the impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice before 2027 stood at 3.40% (vol USD 83 thousand), unchanged against yesterday, a fourth day essentially flat. The methodological caveat is worth more than the number: with USD 83 thousand in accumulated volume, against USD 116.12M in the presidential market, movement in this book does not support a narrative. What is worth recording is the absence of movement in the face of an institutional sequence now four days long and five episodes deep: a foreign head of state attacking a justice by name from a Brazilian campaign platform, the Court's president replying in public, the US government denying any intent to interfere in the election, an ambassador recalled for consultations and now China speaking out on external interference. None of it moved the price. Real money goes on pricing institutional friction, not removal risk.
